title: Tata's HyperVault Plans Rs 70,000-Crore AI Data Centre Campus Near Hyderabad
excerpt: TCS subsidiary acquires 264 acres in Telangana for a 1-gigawatt AI data centre, but key details on power agreements, construction timelines, and anchor tenants remain unconfirmed.
body:
• TCS subsidiary HyperVault has acquired 264 acres near Hyderabad for an AI data centre campus with a planned investment of up to Rs 70,000 crore and capacity of 1 gigawatt.
  • Private equity firm TPG has committed Rs 18,000 crore to support HyperVault's data centre plans, with additional financing details undisclosed.
  • Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has asked for a 21-month completion timeline, targeting a June 2, 2028 inauguration on the state's formation day.
  • Key details including power purchase agreements, environmental clearances, construction contracts, and anchor tenants remain unconfirmed.

India's Largest Announced AI Data Centre

Tata Consultancy Services' data centre subsidiary, HyperVault AI Data Center Limited, has acquired 264 acres in Telangana's Future City near Hyderabad to develop what would be one of India's largest announced AI data centre projects, the company and the Telangana government said on September 5. The facility is designed for up to 1 gigawatt — 1,000 megawatts — of capacity, featuring high-density, liquid-cooled computing infrastructure for advanced AI developers and hyperscale cloud operators.

The project is expected to create approximately 7,000 direct and indirect jobs. HyperVault and the state government said the design includes renewable energy and water-neutral cooling, though neither has released technical specifications or a phased capacity plan.

How HyperVault Was Built

HyperVault was established as a wholly owned TCS subsidiary following a Rs 75 million capital infusion approved by the TCS board in October 2025 and formalized in December 2025 as part of the company's "infrastructure-to-intelligence" initiative. Before the Hyderabad announcement, HyperVault secured Rs 18,000 crore from private equity firm TPG to support its data centre plans, indicating that external capital will play a significant role in the Rs 70,000-crore investment.

A TCS delegation met with Chief Minister Revanth Reddy and Telangana ministers, including IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu, at the state secretariat to finalize the plan. The deal originated from discussions between Telangana officials and Tata leadership at the World Economic Forum in Davos in January 2026.

A Crowded Field of Announcements

Telangana is not new to AI data centre pledges. In January 2025, the state signed a Rs 10,000-crore memorandum of understanding with CtrlS Datacenters for a 400 MW cluster. That was followed by a Rs 10,500-crore agreement with Japan's NTT Data and Neysa Networks in April 2025 for another 400 MW cluster designed for 25,000 GPUs. None of the earlier Telangana projects have reached commissioning.

Other states are competing aggressively. Gujarat signed a Rs 25,000-crore, 250 MW data centre agreement with Larsen & Toubro Vyoma in February 2026. Andhra Pradesh approved four data centre projects in July-August 2026 totaling Rs 2.83 lakh crore across 1,488 acres. Karnataka has announced plans for a green data centre and what it calls the "first and largest AI university," though neither announcement includes investment amounts, capacity, or timelines.

"Large investment announcements in this sector have not consistently resulted in completed, operational capacity within the projected timelines."

— MediaNama analysis

What Remains Unconfirmed

The September 5 announcement omitted several details typical for a project of this scale. These include a signed power purchase agreement for up to 1 GW, land-use and environmental clearances, identification of a construction contractor or EPC partner, confirmation of anchor tenants or hyperscaler commitments, and a breakdown of how the Rs 70,000 crore will be financed among TCS, TPG, and other potential investors.

The state government has committed to expediting regulatory approvals, but as of the announcement, no construction timeline, phased capacity schedule, or environmental clearance status has been made public.

India's AI Spending Gap

India's AI infrastructure investment announcements continue to outpace realized spending. Reliance Industries is constructing a 168 MW facility in Jamnagar that Meta will lease, positioning Reliance as an infrastructure provider rather than a model developer. The contrast between HyperVault's India-focused approach and Meta's global Project Waterworth subsea cable system — spanning over 50,000 km across five continents — illustrates the different scales at which these investments operate. For all the headline figures, the gap between announcement and commissioning remains the defining challenge of India's AI infrastructure ambitions.
